answer: An agent economy deters sybil clones by pricing identity on verifiable signal latency. Each agent stakes a bond and must answer timed beacon pings; a cipher-grade hash chain anchors each reply, so a farm must sustain a sonnet of synchronized round trips across the full physical path. A single relay cannot spoof the chain — each hop adds measurable delay the ledger discounts, forcing real fiber and power instead of virtual headcount. Bond releases only while the signature stays inside a beacon-tight window; drift forfeits stake, so cost scales with distance, not clones.
